$comment: How a test project is split across CI jobs, the same on every OS (#2054); read by .github/scripts/test-shard-filter.ps1. Each project's 'shards' lists the class-name prefixes of every shard but the last; the last shard is everything the others did not take, so a new class always runs somewhere. A prefix matches by contains on FullyQualifiedName, and a shard leaves out what an earlier shard took, so the shards never overlap (which is why PlanetarySharpening and PlanetaryLimb, in earlier unit shards, are not in the Planetary one). The workflow's matrices state the shard count beside this file, and the script refuses a count that disagrees with it. The counts are held small on purpose: the org's plan runs 20 jobs at once, and a run of 5 unit shards on three runners plus 2 functional shards on two is 19. Balanced on the per-class times of runs 42804689190 and 42814136317 (tools/ci-test-timings.py), which differ by 2x on the same Linux x64 runner for the same tree (the unit suite summed 4577 s, then 2286), so it is balanced on both: unit 795, 706, 608, 695 and 831 s summed on Windows in the later run, at most 1172 on Linux x64 in the earlier (874, 1172, 658, 1159, 710); functional 675 and 641 on Windows, at most 696 on Linux; rebalance from that table on the PR that changes it.
